name: Saskatchewan Landing Provincial Park - Riverside and Nighthawk Campgrounds
waterfront_evidence: Split 2026-11-19. Lake Diefenbaker is a reservoir: measured to the high-water edge, taken as the treeline/sand line in front of Riverside's shore row (the SKPP site photos, taken at high water, show the lake lapping at the grass there; the imagery shows the reservoir drawn down, with a sand strip and a vegetated flat beyond). Esri World_Imagery z18 frame (0.38 m/px) and a 3x crop of Riverside with every SKPP GIS site point and 50 m rings: shore-row nightly sites R28 about 15 m, R29 about 19 m, R31-R33 about 25 m and R36-R41 about 30-45 m from that line, all inside a continuous belt of tall trees and shrubs; R1-R24 lie west of the campground road, farther back in woods. SKPP site photos: R28 open grass under scattered trees with the lake beyond a tall-grass fringe; R29 the lake past trunks; R31, R32, R33, R36 and R38 the lake through trees; R40 open grass to a reed band with the water beyond, farther off; R39 and R41 too low-resolution to read. Nighthawk lies across Hwy 261, inland. Every paging row reads 'Near Water - no'. R28 (and perhaps R29) may sit on open ground within 50 m, but the imagery cannot see under the canopy, the photos are undated and the booking data says not near water, so the call stays down: a view through trees from the shore row. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: ReserveAmerica SKPP parkId 290135, read 2026-11-19 (whole-park paging table, 337 rows, + every Riverside and Nighthawk detail page, 60): Riverside 34 Nightly Electric (R1-R12, R14-R24, R28, R29, R31-R33, R36-R41), Nighthawk 26 Nightly Electric (N1, N3, N5, N7-N29) = 60 site-specific sites, all bookable by the night; posted max equipment length 25-65 ft in Riverside (R2, R15 and R28 at 25) and 32-70 ft in Nighthawk. Park map (2026-06-19): both loops off one junction on Highway 261, potable water, washrooms, a playground and an accessible service centre. Its own place about 2 km east of Bearpaw/Sagebrush (centroid to centroid 1.96 km, about 2.4 km by road). A real public drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude
note: Provincial-park campgrounds at the west end of Lake Diefenbaker, about 2 km east of the Hwy 4 bridge off Hwy 261: Riverside in a single row along the shore woods, Nighthawk across the highway from it. Riverside's lake-side sites R28-R41 look at the water through a belt of trees, R28 and R29 the most openly. Showers, laundry and groceries are at Bearpaw. Bearpaw and Sagebrush (the park's main campgrounds) and Bison Hollow have their own entries. --Claude

season.note: 2026 dates. Full services May 14 to September 30; October camping on electric sites booked through the park office, with portable toilets and the park's dump station. No winter camping.

fees.note: $4 a night less from October 1, with reduced services.

name: Saskatchewan Landing Provincial Park - Bison Hollow Campground
waterfront_evidence: Split 2026-11-19. Lake Diefenbaker is a reservoir: measured to the high-water edge, taken as the inner edge of the wave-washed sand band below the loop (the imagery shows the reservoir drawn down, with a vegetated flat and the water 200 m+ beyond). Esri World_Imagery z18 frame (0.38 m/px) and a 1.5x crop with SKPP GIS points of BH14-BH24 and 50 m rings: the south-west row (BH21-BH24) sits about 30-50 m from that edge, with the loop's perimeter track and a strip of shrubs and trees between; the rest of the loop is farther back. SKPP site photos: BH19 and BH20 show the lake in the distance past trees and grass, BH21 faintly through trees; BH22, BH23 and BH24 show only grass and trees. Every paging row reads 'Near Water - no'. A view through and past trees, not a site on open ground to the water. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: ReserveAmerica SKPP parkId 290135, read 2026-11-19 (whole-park paging table, 337 rows, + every Bison Hollow detail page, 24): Bison Hollow 24 Nightly Electric (BH1-BH16, BH18-BH25), all site-specific and bookable by the night, posted max equipment length 32-50 ft; Prairie Meadow's 4 group areas beside it (2 'Group Electric - Small', 2 'Group Electric - Medium') are not counted. Park map (2026-06-19): its own road west of Highway 4, potable water, washrooms, wood, an accessible service centre and a sani dump at the entrance. Its own place about 5 km west of Bearpaw/Sagebrush (centroid to centroid 5.07 km, about 12.5 km by road). A real public drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude
note: Provincial-park campground on the north shore of Lake Diefenbaker west of the Hwy 4 bridge, a single loop in scattered trees above the shore; a few sites see the lake past the trees. Showers, laundry and groceries are at Bearpaw, about 12 km by road. Four Prairie Meadow group areas sit beside it. Bearpaw and Sagebrush (the park's main campgrounds) and Riverside/Nighthawk have their own entries. --Claude
